media_work.title: Anatomy of Innocence: Testimonies of the Wrongfully Convicted
media_work.creator_name: Edited by Laura Caldwell and Leslie S. Klinger
media_work.focus_or_theme: Collection of exoneree stories told by prominent mystery/thriller writers
media_work.key_statistics: Features 14 exonerees; eyewitness misidentifications played a role in 70% of DNA-confirmed exonerations

key_quotes_raw: The stories are variations on Kafkaesque themes: Innocents inexplicably implicated in gruesome crimes, stripped of their humanity in sterile interrogation rooms and jail cells, and denied any actual presumption of innocence in their eventual trials.
Remarkably, most of the exonerees are more upbeat than bitter when freed.
systemic_issues_raw: Unreliable eyewitness testimony (played a role in 70% of DNA-confirmed exonerations)
Incentivized informants (witnesses promised rewards for testimony)
Prosecutorial misconduct (suborning perjurious testimony, withholding information on deals)
Racial bias in the criminal justice system
policy_recommendations_raw: Criminal justice reforms to prevent future miscarriages of justice
Reforms to prevent use of incentivized informants
additional_resources_raw: Life After Innocence project at Loyola University in Chicago (founded by Laura Caldwell)
media_item.item_title: Book Content: Anatomy of Innocence: Testimonies of the Wrongfully Convicted
media_item.focus_or_theme: Collection of exoneree stories told by prominent mystery/thriller writers
media_item.summary_notes: This book features 14 exonerees' stories, each paired with a prominent mystery/thriller writer.  It covers the entire wrongful conviction experience, from arrest to exoneration and life afterward, aiming to provide readers with a deeper understanding of the flawed criminal justice system.
media_item.case_details_raw: The book includes detailed accounts of various wrongful convictions, highlighting the experiences of exonerees from arrest through imprisonment to exoneration and life afterward.  Specific cases include Kirk Bloodsworth (Maryland, death row for rape and murder, exonerated in 1993), Michael Evans (Chicago, Illinois, 26 years served for child murder), Gloria Killian (California, murder), Juan Rivera (Illinois, murder and rape, about 20 years served), Audrey Edmunds, Alton Logan (26 years served), and Jerry Miller (Illinois).

featured_individuals.crime_convicted_of: Rape and murder of a young girl
contributing_factors_raw: Eyewitness misidentification: Identified by two youngsters who had been coached by police
Unreliable forensic science: Later disproven by DNA evidence
featured_individuals.cross_reference: The actual killer was later identified through DNA database as a fellow inmate

contributing_factors_raw: Incentivized informant: Witness was given a $1,250 reward for testimony

research_notes_raw:
The book pairs each exoneree with a prominent mystery or thriller writer to tell their story, including Lee Child, Sara Paretsky, Laurie King, S.J. Rozan, and others. The editors note that apart from "nominal" fees paid to authors, editors, and exonerees, any royalties from the book go to the Life After Innocence project at Loyola University in Chicago.

The book is structured to cover every aspect of the wrongful conviction experience, from arrest through imprisonment to exoneration and life afterward. It aims to give readers "a deeper understanding of the price of our flawed criminal justice system and an urge to help."
